task.description:
Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md. Independently re-derive your verdict from the artefact itself, not from CODE-DESIGNER's own result.summary (which you should treat as a claim to verify, not a fact to copy) -- see core-directives.md's 'Every producing step has a validating step'. Check specifically:
1. Does the design cover every one of ISS-0451's three acceptance criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml): AC1 (a persistent-fault test scenario proving Letflow.Supervisor/Repo/Bandit survive), AC2 (documented restart-intensity arithmetic showing the fix tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle), AC3 (no regression to REQ-219's own AC2 boot-order or AC4 single-crash-isolation tests)?
2. Is the arithmetic in the design actually correct? Work it through yourself rather than trusting the doc's own numbers -- re-derive independently whether the chosen top-level restart-intensity value plus the circuit-breaker's trip threshold genuinely prevents an indefinite persistent fault from ever exhausting the top-level supervisor's budget (not merely delaying it by a bounded, finite number of extra cycles).
3. Does the design contain any implementation code (.ex function bodies)? If it names a new module (e.g. a PollersBreaker GenServer), it should specify signatures/@specs/state-shape/callback contracts only -- fail this check if you find an actual function body implementing logic, not just a signature.
4. Is the design unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without having to invent any missing decision (exact config keys, exact state machine transitions, exact backoff schedule values, exact module/file placement)?
5. Does the design explicitly state how REQ-219's own AC2 (boot order: Infrastructure before Pollers) and AC4 (single Pollers-budget-exhaustion event still leaves Infrastructure/Http alone) are preserved, with reasoning you can independently verify against the current code (lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex)?
6. Is the specified regression-test mechanism (how the test keeps the fault persistent, unlike REQ-219's own AC4 test which clears it) concrete enough for TEST-DESIGNER to build without design ambiguity?

This is a hard gate -- FAIL with specific, itemized gaps (per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's validator-fail worked example) if any check above doesn't pass; do not rubber-stamp.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict states explicitly, per ISS-0451 AC, whether AC1/AC2/AC3 are each covered by the design
Verdict states the validator's own independently re-derived arithmetic check result, not a repetition of CODE-DESIGNER's numbers
Verdict states explicitly whether any implementation code was found in the design doc
Verdict states explicitly whether REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation reasoning is checked and correct
A FAIL verdict lists every gap by section/line with what must change; a PASS verdict states what was independently re-derived and how
